title: A diferencia de: comparar dos casos

sections.content: A diferencia de (unlike, in contrast to) opens a direct comparison between two cases -- exactly what this lesson needs to hold Cárdenas next to Perón point by point: personal style, social base, and lasting reputation. It's followed by a noun phrase, not a full clause. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: A diferencia del carismático coronel argentino, Cárdenas era conocido por un estilo personal más bien discreto, casi austero.
items.english: Unlike the charismatic Argentine colonel, Cárdenas was known for a rather understated, almost austere personal style.

items.spanish: A diferencia de Perón, que construyó su poder principalmente sobre el movimiento obrero urbano, Cárdenas se apoyó de manera decisiva en el campesinado.
items.english: Unlike Perón, who built his power mainly on the urban labor movement, Cárdenas relied decisively on the peasantry.

items.spanish: A diferencia de lo que muchos analistas internacionales predijeron, esta medida no provocó el colapso económico que se temía.
items.english: Unlike what many international analysts predicted, this measure didn't cause the economic collapse that was feared.

items.spanish: A diferencia también del peronismo, el legado de Cárdenas resulta mucho más ampliamente reconocido y celebrado dentro de México.
items.english: Also unlike Peronism, Cárdenas's legacy turns out to be much more widely recognized and celebrated within Mexico.

sections.content: A diferencia de lo que + verb (as in the third example) is a handy variant for contrasting with an expectation or prediction rather than another person or thing -- lo que stands in for "what [people expected/predicted]."
